DischargeLoop is exploring a human-accountable operating layer for care transitions. The starting point is deliberately specific: one service line, a visible exception queue, and a measured reason to change the workflow. Expansion across service lines, post-acute networks and risk-bearing groups depends on permission, repeatable onboarding and demonstrated operational value.

01 / FIELD NOTE
01 / Establish the operating context

Ask the transitions director which service line to map, which role owns the workflow and who controls the relevant budget. Separate the buyer, the person doing the work and the oversight owner. Do not assume they are the same person.

02 / FIELD NOTE
02 / Follow one handoff

Walk through a contact, referral or evidence exception using a process description. Identify where a status first becomes uncertain, which system holds the source and what the receiving team sees. Do not bring patient records to the website or audit inquiry form.

03 / FIELD NOTE
03 / Trace the next responsibility

Name the responsible role, its next action, the escalation rule and the evidence needed for closure. A task assignment is not resolution. Distinguish request, confirmation, attendance and documented closure.

04 / FIELD NOTE
04 / Compare with the current process

Map calls, fax, EHR tasks and referral platforms. Ask whether existing software already closes the same exception at comparable active staff effort. If so, there may be no case for another queue.

05 / FIELD NOTE
05 / Agree the next decision

A useful outcome may be a bounded retrospective map—or a decision to stop. Before reviewing a cohort, establish an operations sponsor, permitted data route, security review and explicit human oversight.

Leave with a service line, a defined exception, an owner, an evidence question and a next decision. No patient data is needed to request the conversation.

01 / FIELD NOTE
Define the unit of work

Agree the episode definition, eligibility criteria, exclusions and the observation window. Keep still-open and censored cases visible. Record the cohort denominator and the evidence source before calculating any summary.

02 / FIELD NOTE
Separate effort from elapsed time

The brief’s primary metric is median staff minutes from discharge to documented handoff closure versus baseline. Clarify whether this means total active staff effort during that interval. Track elapsed discharge-to-closure duration separately.

Choose the baseline

Observe the current EHR, referral and manual workflow over a defined baseline window. Record decision-maker roles and incumbent contracts. A synthetic interface cannot supply an observed baseline.

Keep the guardrails

Track unreachable-case escalation completion and erroneous closure count. A faster-looking queue is not useful if it drops difficult episodes or labels unresolved work complete.

05 / FIELD NOTE
Set the review gate

The sponsor and operating reviewers define acceptable thresholds, escalation timing, scope and the time box. Do not import a clinical or financial benchmark from a demonstration.

No operational gain, clinical benefit or billing validity is established by an empty scorecard. The purpose is to define what evidence an evaluation would need.

01 / FIELD NOTE
Clinical workflow context

CMS TCM guidance defines a service and its documentation requirements. AHRQ MATCH and RED describe medication reconciliation and discharge tasks. These support separating source differences, contact attempts, appointments and human review.

02 / FIELD NOTE
Data access is a separate question

CMS event-notification guidance has a defined scope. A notification does not give a new vendor universal data rights. Confirm the recipient, source owner, identity rules, freshness and permissible use before any later pilot.

03 / FIELD NOTE
Existing alternatives matter

Bamboo Health markets automated transitions with outreach and human escalation. CarePort markets referral workflows. These are vendor descriptions, not evidence that DischargeLoop offers a capability they lack.

04 / FIELD NOTE
Demand remains unproven

The supplied brief classifies support for the workflow and competition as moderate, while willingness to switch or pay remains low-evidence. No customer, revenue, ROI or pricing acceptance is established.

Use the source register below to inspect the original guidance. Interpret clinical, privacy and billing requirements with the appropriate professional reviewers.

A DELIBERATELY SPECIFIC BEGINNING
One service line.
A measured reason to change.

Make the unfinished handoff visible.
Keep the decision with the care team.

The proposed first product is a discharge-event exception queue: unsent outreach, appointment-closure status, attributed evidence and named reviewers. Five distinct module directions preserve the responsibilities around that episode.

This is a research-stage concept. No operating product, revenue, adoption, clinical outcome, live integration or pricing acceptance is established.

Expansion across service lines, post-acute networks and risk-bearing groups depends on permission, incumbent differentiation and repeatable operational value. No dollar TAM or guaranteed savings is claimed.

02
PRINCIPLES THAT SHAPE THE INTERFACE
Human accountability, made concrete.
01
Source before certainty

A status should be inspectable. Missing and contradictory evidence can remain unresolved.

02
An owner before an action

Make the receiving role and next review visible. Assignment is not completion.

03
Permission before expansion

No live pilot without data rights, security approval and human oversight.

04
Evidence before scale

Compare with the existing workflow, keep the denominator and accept a decision to stop.

03
LEARNING FROM THE OPERATING REALITY
The next conversation is with the team.
Regional hospital associations

Introduce a transitions director and a single service line to map.

ACO operations peers

Explore attribution, cross-setting responsibility and receiving-team workflows.

Post-acute referral partners

Examine the handoff, acceptance evidence and information gaps.

EHR implementation partners

Establish whether a permitted source route and operating gap are practical.

These are proposed routes to learning, not claimed customers, integrations or partnerships. No unverified team biographies, endorsements or company profiles are presented.

01
Research-stage scope

The website demonstrates proposed care-transitions responsibilities and fictional product states. Product names, operating scope, demand, pricing acceptance, integrations and legal clearance remain to be validated.

02
Synthetic demonstration

The demo contains fictional names, dates, source references and review history. Local acknowledgement controls add resettable simulation notes without contacting people or writing to an external clinical, administrative or payment system.

03
No clinical or billing determination

The content is not diagnosis, treatment, medication advice, coding guidance, a determination of service eligibility, or reimbursement assurance. Appropriate professional reviewers must interpret actual clinical, privacy, security and billing requirements.

04
Commercial hypotheses

The displayed $2,500 per facility per month and $5,000 setup fee are hypothetical test prices, not active offers or accepted terms. There is no checkout, payment collection, automatic renewal or active subscription through this website.

05
Accounts and inquiries

Customer accounts are not available. Sign-in, secure-link and access-help controls are isolated frontend previews, with no authentication or email service. Inquiry controls do not submit requests or schedule a meeting.

06
Original materials and references

Brand assets, diagrams and interface examples were prepared for this concept. Locally hosted fonts retain their licence notices. Third-party guidance and vendor pages are linked as references; their names do not imply endorsement or a commercial relationship.

07
Before a live pilot

Written scope, an operations sponsor, authorised source rights, security approval, human oversight, evaluation measures and a review gate are prerequisites. A separate reviewed agreement would be required before any operating service or paid pilot.

01
Complete still states

The route is fully drawn, draft text is complete, and all meaningful content remains visible. A system reduced-motion preference is respected.

02
Native page movement

There is no scroll trap or replacement scroll engine. Links and menus provide direct routes around the extended homepage story.

03
Motion with a purpose

Drawing connects sources and responsibilities; typing reveals an unsent draft. No animated metric implies measured performance.

02
KEYBOARD, READING AND TOUCH
Several ways through the same workflow.
01
Keyboard navigation

Use Tab to reach links, controls and forms. Native buttons activate with Enter or Space. Dialogs close with Escape; tabs expose selected states.

02
Readable labels and evidence

Status text accompanies semantic color. Source identifiers, reviewer roles, dates and limitations remain available as real text.

03
Mobile reading order

The workbench and evidence stack into ordinary document flow. No required explanation exists only in a hover state.

04
Visible focus

Interactive controls have visible focus outlines. Native form labels and validation support the request and access previews.

03
SCOPE OF THE CHECKED PREVIEW
Accessibility is a continuing review.
What has been implemented

Responsive layouts, native controls, labelled inputs, reduced-motion handling, skip links, dialog behavior, text contrast adaptation and alternatives to motion-dependent content.

What is not claimed

No independent accessibility certification or exhaustive assistive-technology audit is represented. A production launch needs broader browser, device and assistive-technology testing.
